Per-token weight bytes for the ds4-min decode workload.

This file is the example of where a cost model's numbers come from. Every line
is computed from a tensor's shape and element format as the GGUF records them,
multiplied by how many times a token reads it. Nothing here was measured by a
profiler, and nothing here could have been: a capture records no shapes.

Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-IQ2XXS-w2Q2K-AProjQ8-SExpQ8-OutQ8-chat-v2-imatrix-0731
Layers: 43. Even layers (21) carry the compressor and indexer paths.

Block sizes, bytes per block, elements per block:
  Q8_0      34 bytes / 32 elements
  Q2_K      84 bytes / 256 elements
  IQ2_XXS   66 bytes / 256 elements
  F16        2 bytes / element
  F32        4 bytes / element

So for a [cols,rows] tensor:
  Q8_0(cols,rows)    = (cols/32)*34  * rows
  Q2_K(cols,rows,n)  = (cols/256)*84 * rows * n
  IQ2_XXS(cols,rows,n) = (cols/256)*66 * rows * n
  F16(cols,rows)     = cols*rows*2

Each of the totals above is the indexer-ACTIVE figure (pos >= 2051). With the
indexer inactive, drop indexer.attn_q_b (352,321,536) and indexer.proj
(11,010,048):

  weight families  9,196,595,200   vs  9,559,926,784 active
  TOTAL            9,238,107,464   vs  9,601,439,048 active

Any of these four numbers quoted without its position regime is one of the other
three 3.8% of the time.

RESIDENCY

Everything read out of the mmap'd GGUF is host-page-table resident: the GPU
reads those pages through host page tables and nothing copies them to device
memory. The KV/compressed-cache activation line is the sole exception -- those
buffers are cudaMalloc'd and device-resident. So the residency partition is:

  host page table  9,561,986,376   everything except the KV line
  device              39,452,672   KV/compressed-cache activation reads
  TOTAL            9,601,439,048

The residency partition is not the weight/activation split, and this is the
trap this file exists to demonstrate. Host-page-table bytes are 9,561,986,376;
the four weight families are 9,559,926,784. They differ by 2,059,592 bytes -- the
per-layer norms/sinks/bias and the mixed line, which are mmap'd like every other
weight but are not one of the four quantized families. 0.022% apart, and
distinguishable by nothing except knowing which question was asked.

That matters because these bytes get divided by a measured time to cross-check a
ceiling, and only one of the three plausible numerators is the right population:

  numerator (bytes / 0.05894 s, the ablated-C end-to-end decode time)
  weights only                  162.20 GB/s      inside -- but by coincidence of size
  host-page-table resident      162.23 GB/s      inside -- and the correct population
  all bytes                     162.90 GB/s      OUTSIDE, because it charges
                                                 device-resident KV reads to a
                                                 host-page-table ceiling

Use the host-page-table figure. "Weights" agrees with it to 0.02% here only
because the two non-family mmap'd lines are small; nothing makes that stable, and
a model that reaches for "weights" is right by accident.

A Table splitting this file per kernel must therefore charge the KV line to a
separate DeviceResident entry. Give every line one residency stamp and the
contamination is inside an aggregate, where EvaluatedCoverage cannot see it.

WHAT THIS FILE IS NOT

It is keyed by weight family, not by kernel symbol, so it is not directly a
Table: nothing here says which kernel reads attn_q_b. Turning it into a Table
requires a second mapping, from kernel symbol to the tensors that kernel reads,
which likewise is not in any capture and has to come from the code that
launches the kernel.

It also double-counts nothing and deduplicates nothing across kernels: if two
kernels read the same weight in one token, attributing the full bytes to both
would overstate the total. A per-kernel Table must decide where each read is
charged.
